skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render MP4 videos from React/Remotion TSX components using the inference.sh CLI, with options for resolution, frame rate, duration, props, and codec.
skill.summary: Create Remotion-based MP4 renders from React component code through the inference.sh cloud renderer.
skill.author: inference-sh-9

security_audit.summary: The skill appears to be a legitimate Remotion rendering workflow, but it depends on the inference.sh CLI and cloud renderer. The quick start includes a curl-to-shell installer, which is a confirmed critical supply-chain risk. Most Markdown backtick detections are false positives, while CLI examples and remote rendering remain real trust boundaries.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the pipe-to-shell command with manual download, checksum verification, and an explicit install command.

remediation.issue: Component code and props are sent to an external renderer.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to include secrets, credentials, private customer data, or proprietary code without approval.

remediation.issue: Related examples recommend installing additional skills with npx.
remediation.suggestion: Mark related skills as optional and tell users to review each skill before installation.

content.user_title: Render Remotion Videos from React Components
content.value_statement: React teams need a repeatable way to turn component animations into video files. This skill sends Remotion TSX to inference.sh and returns MP4 renders with configurable output settings.
actual_capabilities: Runs the infsh Remotion renderer with user supplied TSX component code.
Supports Remotion imports such as AbsoluteFill, Sequence, spring, and interpolate.
Passes props into the rendered component for data-driven video output.
Configures width, height, frames per second, duration, and codec.
Shows CLI and Python SDK workflows, including streaming progress updates.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI or SDK and an authenticated account.
Sends component code and props to an external rendering service.
Only documented Remotion and React imports are shown in the skill examples.
Does not include local rendering, asset packaging, or post-production editing.

output_examples.input: Create a three second fade-in title animation.
output_examples.output: Returns an MP4 video link with a centered title that fades from transparent to fully visible.

output_examples.input: Render a square progress counter for social media.
output_examples.output: Returns a 1080 square MP4 with animated percentage text and the requested frame rate.

output_examples.input: Render a branded sequence with title and subtitle props.
output_examples.output: Returns an MP4 that applies the supplied text props inside the Remotion component.

best_practices: Review all TSX before sending it to the external renderer.
Keep props free of secrets, credentials, private customer data, and unreleased source material.
Set duration, frame rate, and dimensions explicitly for repeatable renders.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote install scripts to a shell without manual verification.
Do not include API keys or private tokens in component code or props.
Do not install related skills automatically during a render workflow.

faq.question: What does this skill render?
faq.answer: It renders React and Remotion TSX component code into MP4 video files through inference.sh.

faq.question: Does it run locally?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow uses the inference.sh CLI or SDK and an external rendering service.

faq.question: Can I pass custom data into a video?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports props that are passed into the exported Remotion component.

faq.question: Which output settings are supported?
faq.answer: The examples show width, height, frames per second, duration, composition ID, props, and codec.

faq.question: What should I avoid sending?
faq.answer: Avoid secrets, credentials, private customer data, and proprietary code that is not approved for external processing.

faq.question: Why is the install command risky?
faq.answer: The quick start pipes a remote script into sh, so users cannot inspect the installer before execution.
